content.introduction: The sources indicate that the S&P 500 (SPX) breadth is down to 44.11% from 47.80%, the CCMP fell to 39.51% from 42.04%, and the RUT dropped to 48.80% from 51.61%. The outlook is incrementally bullish as the index is above mid-August highs, with the next hurdle being the all-time high of 14,655 from June 22nd. The Equity OIPCR remains unchanged at 0.78, implying retail traders' bullishness is stable but less than in Q1. The S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, and Dow Industrials are down weekly but have positive year-to-date returns, while the Russell 2000 is also down weekly but shows a positive year-to-date return.

The normally very stable Equity OIPCR is unchanged again at 0.78 versus 0.78 last week. This ratio is now 2 ticks above its lowest level since mid-July. At this level it implies that equity option traders (which includes a lot of retail traders) remain about as bullish as last week, though less bullish than in Q1.
